html:
The Managua earthquake struck the capital of Nicaragua just after midnight on 23 December 1972. It killed about 10,000 people and destroyed most of the city centre.

The quake was not very large, but it struck directly under Managua, and its adobe and brick buildings collapsed. Fires burned for days, and hundreds of thousands lost their homes. The old centre was never rebuilt; the city grew outward in scattered neighbourhoods, and the ruined cathedral still stands.

Aid poured in from abroad, but Anastasio Somoza Debayle, son of Somoza García, and his circle took much of it and profited from the rebuilding. Even business leaders turned against the family. The anger fed support for the Sandinistas and the revolution that followed. It is the turning point of late Somoza Nicaragua, as Mitch was for later decades.
sum: The Managua earthquake struck the capital of Nicaragua just after midnight on 23 December 1972. It killed about 10,000 people and destroyed most of the city centre.
